DO NOT WRITE IN ANY BARCODES. There are thirty questions on this paper. Answer all questions. For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. In their transition to market economies some former command economies have adopted a gradual approach. This has meant continuing with some of the features of their command system. What is not a valid, short-run reason for continuing with the feature shown? feature reason for continuation

options.A: inconvertible currency to attract foreign direct investment
options.B: price controls on foodstuffs to protect the real value of workers’ incomes
options.C: state ownership of banks to avoid large-scale bankruptcies
options.D: tariffs on imported manufactures to allow comparative advantage to develop

questions.questionText: A country is producing electrical goods and medicines at full capacity. An innovation is developed that enables the country to produce a new medicine which becomes in great demand. How would this be represented by its production possibility curves? electrical Z X goods Y W O medicines

options.A: as a movement from W to X
options.B: as a movement from X to Y
options.C: as a movement from X to Z
options.D: as a movement from Y to X

questions.questionText: What would encourage the growth of the international division of labour?

options.A: an improvement in transport systems
options.B: instability in international exchange rates
options.C: restrictions on the movement of resources
options.D: the widespread introduction of tariffs

questions.questionText: What would not cause the demand curve for foreign holidays to shift to the left?

options.A: a fall in consumers’ disposable income
options.B: a fall in the price of domestic holidays
options.C: a rise in advertising of domestic holidays
options.D: a rise in the price of foreign holidays

questions.questionText: A movement along a supply curve for a product is likely to occur if there is a rise in

options.A: the demand for a complementary product.
options.B: the distribution costs of the product.
options.C: the subsidy a producer receives for producing the product.
options.D: the wages of the employees who produce the product.

questions.questionText: A firm makes televisions. What does the elasticity of supply for the firm represent?

options.A: the need to increase production because of a successful advertising campaign
options.B: the possibility of switching production from other goods the firm makes to televisions
options.C: the speed at which additional fixed factors used to produce televisions can be obtained
options.D: the way the firm’s production changes as a result of a change in price of televisions

questions.questionText: Demand and supply in a competitive market both decrease by 10% at all prices. What will be the effect on the equilibrium price and quantity sold? price quantity sold

options.A: 10% decrease 10% decrease
options.B: 10% decrease no change
options.C: 5% decrease 5% decrease
options.D: no change 10% decrease

questions.questionText: Between 2006 and 2007, the price of skimmed milk powder on the world market rose from $1000 per tonne to $2400 per tonne. Assuming that the market is a free market, what will result from the price change?

options.A: Consumers will buy more complements to skimmed milk powder.
options.B: Farmers will increase the size of their dairy herds to supply more milk.
options.C: Firms processing milk into skimmed milk will switch to producing substitutes.
options.D: Governments will introduce a system of rationing.

questions.questionText: A local council runs a museum. It used to charge an admission fee. It decided to give free entry in the hope of encouraging more people to use the museum and find out about the history of its area which the council regards as being important. What can be said about the museum?

options.A: It is a merit good because it is believed to be worth greater attendance.
options.B: It is a merit good because it is run by the local council.
options.C: It is a public good because anyone can use the museum.
options.D: It is a public good because people do not now have to pay for admission

What will be the effect of the changes in the oil price on a country’s Consumer Price Index and on its inflation rate in Year 2 compared with Year 1? effect on the effect on the Consumer Price Index rate of inflation

options.A: decrease decrease

questions.questionText: Why is a deficit on the current account of the balance of payments in economies with freely floating exchange rates often thought to be an economic problem?

options.A: It implies a net outflow of capital from the economy.
options.B: It involves borrowing from abroad.
options.C: It leads to increases in unemployment.
options.D: It results in a loss of foreign exchange reserves.

questions.questionText: In which situation must a country’s balance of trade in goods and services improve?

options.A: Export costs rise more than import costs.
options.B: Export prices rise more than import prices.
options.C: Export revenues rise more than import revenues.
options.D: Export volumes rise more than import volumes.
